lens: Editorial and brand craft — narrow mobile viewport; simulated AI expertise, not a human participant
reason: The public presentation has an authored engineering-document identity: legible mobile display type, restrained blue/orange hierarchy, numbered sections, hairline rows and clearly differentiated client/student actions. The real PwC-visit photograph is accurately captioned as member activity rather than project evidence. However, the consulting proposition still lacks inspectable engagement proof, and the narrow-mobile sequence spends substantial space explaining process before showing credibility. Those are material editorial limits to a world-class claim. I traced the client journey from services and fee FAQ to the contact form, its confirmation/error states and server email handoff. Supplied desktop/mobile tests record that journey passing, but intercept the contact API; this is local synthetic evidence, not observed user success or delivered email. Release readiness across the public/private product remains unproven within this seat’s scope.

findings.evidence: The captured Selected work section contains industry-level prose, a pending-client-approval status and six organization names/logos. PUBLIC_PROJECTS is empty; /work/page.tsx:56-63 omits Selected work when no approved projects exist. The member photograph at home/page.tsx:134-136 is a PwC visit, not a consulting artifact.
findings.userImpact: A prospective client can inspect who MECG has worked with and the promised process, but cannot judge the quality or specificity of an actual recommendation or deliverable.
findings.suggestedFix: Have content owners obtain approval for one concise engagement: client question, constraints, method, redacted deliverable image and factual handoff/result. Feature it before process exposition. Preserve the honest pending status until approval; do not invent an outcome.

findings.evidence: At the supplied 390px capture, the stacked hero and complete engagement bench occupy approximately the first 1,400px before organization figures. The bench at line 48 renders all four station controls and a readout; section 04 later repeats all four ENGAGEMENT_STEPS with their outputs.
findings.userImpact: A narrow-screen reader traverses a large process explanation before seeing credibility, then encounters the same explanation again. This weakens the intended proof-first editorial hierarchy.
findings.suggestedFix: On narrow viewports, place the organization/engagement proof before the full bench, or provide a compact bench disclosure. Retain one complete four-step explanation and use the later section for complementary terms rather than repeating its copy.
